the enzyme catalyzing the transsulfuration of 4-l-histidine and cysteine to ovothiol has been identified and characterized.

(1) the transsulfuration reaction that forms the intermediate, 4-mercaptol-histidine, in the biosynthesis pathway of ovothiols is catalyzed by a pyridoxal-phosphate dependent transsulfuration enzyme; (2) S-(4'-histidyl)-l- cysteine sulfoxid is an intermediate in the pathway; (3) the sulfoxide is converted to 4-meraptol-histidine

the biosynthesis of the ovothiol, ovothiol-A, in C. fasciculata is a two-step process that involves the transsulfuration of histidine and cysteine to S-(4'-histidyl)-l -cysteine sulfoxiide, followed by a lyase reaction that cleaves the sulfoxide bond, producing 4-mercaptol-histidine and pyruvate.

the biosynthesis of a novel thiol, ovothiol, from cysteine and histidine in the presence of pyridoxyl phosphate, Fe2+, O2 and a sulfhydryl compound.
the biosynthesis of the unusual ovothiol (N1-methy1-4-mercaptobistidine) in C. fasciculata.

the biosynthesis of the sulfur-containing amino acid ovothiol is initiated by the condensation of cysteine and histidine in the presence of pyridoxalphosphate, oxygen and ferrous ion.
